title: Universal property of an affine unsharpened monoid spectrum
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, and let $A(P)=(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P,\widetilde P)$ be its unsharpened monoid spectrum [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Let $T$ be any topological space with a sheaf $\mathcal A$ of commutative monoids. A local morphism $(T,\mathcal A)\to A(P)$ means a continuous map $f:T\to\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$ together with compatible homomorphisms $\widetilde P(U)\to\mathcal A(f^{-1}U)$ for open $U$, such that each stalk homomorphism $\widetilde P_{f(t)}\to\mathcal A_t$ is local: its inverse image of the units is the units. No sharpness assumption is made on $P$ or on the stalks of $\mathcal A$. Pullback of canonical global sections, using $\Gamma(A(P),\widetilde P)=P$, gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{loc}}((T,\mathcal A),A(P))\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Mon}}(P,\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)).$$
This bijection is natural in $(T,\mathcal A)$ under local morphisms and in $P$ under monoid homomorphisms.

proof.text: The global-sections functor is contravariant: Gamma(k followed by f)=Gamma(f) followed by Gamma(k). Taking the underlying monoid homomorphisms and composing with the canonical numerator sections proves affinePullback(k followed by f)=Gamma(k) composed with affinePullback(f), by associativity. The private Lean helper proves this for all sheafed-space morphisms, without locality assumptions.

proof.text: Apply the surjectivity just proved with T=A(Q) and phi=affineSection(Q) composed with v, obtaining a local g. The preceding composition identity, its prescribed pullback equality, and associativity give affinePullback(f followed by g)=affinePullback(f) composed with v for every local f. Any other g satisfying the displayed conjunction has the same numerator pullback, so the injectivity already proved makes it equal to g. This proves the unique-existence and monoid-naturality clause. No separate spectrum-map construction or composite-locality theorem is required for the statement.

Step 4: the smallest neighborhood D(b) with P_b=P-F gives the stalk, and the unit criterion p in F holds on both sides, so the stalk map is local. Steps 5-6: the prime map and the map on each D(a) are forced, and λ_0=φ. Step 7: naturality in both variables and functoriality of A(u) via Step 5, which is what the citer lem-trf-saturated-blowup-product-charts step 6 uses. Edge cases checked: T empty, P a group, P=0, P=N with a unit or nonunit value, nonintegral target stalks, V_a empty, empty generating tuple.
